brand.name: Alethea
brand.footer: Open-source, evidence-based fact-checking. Greek ἀλήθεια — truth, the absence of forgetting.

hero.headline: Paste a link. See the evidence.
hero.subline: Alethea reads a social-media post, asks the right questions, gathers sources, and shows you exactly how it reached its verdict. No black box. Skeptical by default — if the evidence is thin, we say so.

promise.title: Three promises
promise.skeptical: Skeptical by default — we'd rather say 'we don't know' than guess.
promise.transparent: Show our work — every verdict expands into the full agent transcript.
promise.open: Open source — anyone can run the same check and see the same logic.

howItWorks.title: How Alethea reaches a verdict
howItWorks.pipeline: Five stages, every one visible to you

stages.scrape: We fetch the page or social-media post you submitted. URLs are validated; we never touch internal-network addresses.
stages.extract: A small model condenses the post + any images into a list of testable claims. Opinions and jokes are filtered out.
stages.investigate: N independent investigators each search the open web. They cite by source ID — they can't invent URLs because we hand them the source pool.
stages.judge: A stronger model synthesizes the N reports into one final verdict. Below a confidence floor we mark the claim 'Unverifiable' rather than guess.
stages.explain: Every verdict ships with the full agent transcript, every cited URL, the dissent vector across investigators, and a separate panel that interprets the post's intent (clearly labeled as interpretation, not fact).

verdicts.title: Seven verdict categories
verdicts.misleading: Contains truth but missing critical context.
verdicts.unverifiable: Cannot be verified with available sources.
